title: fix(app-shell): "Add filter" in the Studio list-view inspector adds a row that can be edited
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zhuangjianguo"} -->
_Requested by **Steedos** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_018ETKaNwMZCNRYD7D8Q9Ubb?thread=cmsg_018ETKaNwMZCNRYD7D8Q9UbbU2U5PMGb7vt7eH4fiuXwNj)_

Fixes #26738

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**:Studio 列表视图检查器(以及标签页预设)里的筛选器控件,现在自己保存「还没填完」的条件行。点「Add filter」会出现一行可编辑的条件;填完之后才把这条规则写进视图。
- **为什么改**:控件以前每次渲染都从已保存的规则重新生成行,而保存端的折叠(`foldFilterGroupToSpecRules`)会正确地丢掉未填完的行,于是新加的空行在下一次渲染就消失了,Studio 里根本无法给列表视图加筛选。
- **风险与回滚**:低。只改 app-shell 一个控件的状态持有方式;保存规则不变(未填完的条件仍然不会写进视图),不新增任何元数据键,spec 不动。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- **先看**:`ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/widgets.tsx` 里 `FilterBuilderField` 的 `draft` / `seededFrom` 两个状态和 `handle` 里新增的「与已存规则相同则不写」判断;新测试 `widgets.filterBuilderHeldRow-26738.test.tsx`。
- **两分钟验证**:`cd ui && pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/widgets.filterBuilderHeldRow-26738.test.tsx`,预期 4 个用例全绿;或在 Studio Interfaces 打开某对象的列表视图检查器,Filter →「Add filter」,出现一行,填入值后视图草稿里出现该 filter。
- **需要你做的**:无,席位落地。

## What changes

`FilterBuilderField` (the `filter-builder` widget the Studio list-view inspector's Filter row uses, and the per-tab filter of `filter-mode` tab presets) built the `FilterBuilder`'s row group from the stored rules on every render. The builder's "Add filter" inserts a blank row; the save-side fold drops a row that is not complete yet, as it must; the host stored the unchanged rules and re-rendered, and the re-derived group replaced the builder's rows, so the new row disappeared before it could be edited.

The widget now holds the builder's row group in its own state:

- every builder change is folded; a refused fold (OR over several rows, a nested group) still toasts and writes nothing;
- an accepted fold updates the held rows, and writes only when the folded rules differ from what is stored. An incomplete row therefore stays on screen and writes nothing; completing it writes exactly the complete rule;
- when the stored rules change and are not the echo of this builder's own write (another editor, a reload), the held rows are re-seeded from what is stored. The comparison keys on the rules' JSON, never on an array's identity.

`viewFilterFold.ts` is unchanged: what is persisted is decided by the same fold as before.

## Tests

New `widgets.filterBuilderHeldRow-26738.test.tsx` mounts the real `filter-builder` widget in a host that writes the way `ObjectListViewInspector` does (a new body object on every `onChange`, `filter` dropped when empty):

- "Add filter" adds an editable row, writes nothing while it is incomplete, and completing it writes `[{ field: 'title', operator: 'equals', value: 'open' }]` with the row still on screen;
- a second, incomplete row is held beside a stored rule without a write;
- a stored filter shows as its row and summary, opening it writes nothing, and editing the value away and back writes the stored rule unchanged (round-trip);
- CONTROL: a stored filter changed from outside re-seeds the rows.

Reverse verification (one-off, not kept): with the fix committed, `widgets.tsx` restored to base `c8583f80` in the working tree only (`groupOfStoredRules` occurrences 3 → 0) made the new file red, Tests 3 failed | 1 passed (4); each red is the vanished row ("expected [] to have a length of 1 but got +0"). The round-trip case is green on base too, as a preservation pin should be. Restored with `git checkout HEAD -- …` (occurrences back to 3, `git diff HEAD` empty).

## Acceptance notes

- The card suspected a regression from the filter-fold work of #26306 / #26348. Those changed the builder's value types, not how this widget feeds the builder; the re-derived group predates them in the code read here. History was not walked (shallow checkout), so when it started is not measured.
- The inspector's write callback rebuilds the view body on every `onChange`, so before this change an incomplete row would also have written an unchanged body back to the draft. The widget now writes only when the folded rules change.
- The popover's held rows live as long as the widget is mounted, so closing and reopening the popover keeps an incomplete row ("held until complete").
